title: Effective descent of finite schemes on an etale stack presentation
statement: Let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over a scheme $S$, in the stack and 2-fibre-product conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and let $a:T\to\mathcal X$ be a surjective etale scheme atlas. Put $T_2=T\times_{\mathcal X}T$ and $T_3=T\times_{\mathcal X}T\times_{\mathcal X}T$, with their projections. A finite scheme over $T$ means a scheme $Z$ with a finite morphism $Z\to T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Give such a $Z$ an isomorphism $\theta:p_1^*Z\simeq p_2^*Z$ over $T_2$ satisfying $p_{23}^*\theta\circ p_{12}^*\theta=p_{13}^*\theta$ over $T_3$. Pullback induces an equivalence between the category of morphisms $\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$ representable by finite schemes and the category of these finite schemes with descent datum, including all compatible morphisms. Here representable by finite schemes means that every base change by a scheme is a finite scheme over that scheme. The resulting $\mathcal Y$ is Deligne--Mumford. If $Z$ is normal, meaning that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], then $\mathcal Y$ is normal in the sense that it admits a normal etale scheme atlas. No normality, smoothness or normalization hypothesis is imposed on $\mathcal X$.

source.place: Tags 0245 (lemma-affine) and 02LA (lemma-descending-property-finite); stack-presentation extension via stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06WV (lemma-quasi-coherent-algebraic-stack), part (1). Agent-formulated finite-algebra consequence, not a verbatim assertion about stacks in 0245.

proof.text: Write $b:Z\to T$. By the definition of finite, $b$ is affine. Let $M=b_*\mathcal O_Z$, a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_T$-algebra by the affine-algebra anti-equivalence. On a scheme chart $V\to T_2$, its two pullbacks are the structure algebras of the two pullbacks of $Z$, by relative-spectrum base change. Thus $\theta$ induces an algebra isomorphism $\theta^\sharp:p_2^*M\to p_1^*M$, compatible on all charts. Set $\delta=(\theta^\sharp)^{-1}$. Applying the contravariant structure-algebra functor to the given cocycle gives $\theta_{13}^\sharp=\theta_{12}^\sharp\circ\theta_{23}^\sharp$, hence $\delta_{23}\circ\delta_{12}=\delta_{13}$. This is a module descent datum on $M$, including its algebra operations; no assertion that $T_2$ is a scheme is used.

source.place: Tag 01SA (lemma-affine-equivalence-algebras), with Constructions Tag 01LX (lemma-spec-properties)(2); apply on scheme charts of the presentation.

proof.text: Apply quasi-coherent module descent to $(M,\delta)$. Obtain a cartesian quasi-coherent module $\mathcal A$ on $\mathcal X$ and an isomorphism $\lambda:a^*\mathcal A\simeq M$ respecting the given datum. The tensor and unit compatibilities of this equivalence identify the descent data of $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ with those of $M\otimes M$ and $\mathcal O_T$.

Multiplication $M\otimes M\to M$ and the unit $\mathcal O_T\to M$ commute with $\delta$, since the overlap maps are algebra isomorphisms. Fullness in module descent therefore gives maps $\mu:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ and $e:\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal A$. The two associativity maps from $\mathcal A^{\otimes3}$ have equal restrictions, namely $m(m\otimes1)=m(1\otimes m)$ on $M$; faithfulness makes them equal. The left-unit, right-unit and commutativity equations follow by the same equality test, using the stated unit and symmetry comparisons. Thus each $\mathcal A_x$ is a commutative unital quasi-coherent algebra, with cartesian algebra pullbacks, and $\lambda$ is an algebra isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06WV (lemma-quasi-coherent-algebraic-stack)(1),(5), elementary transport of algebra operations through the tensor-compatible equivalence.

proof.text: For every $x\in\mathcal X(U)$ put $P_x=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_U(\mathcal A_x)$. For an arrow $\alpha:y\to x$ over $u:V\to U$, the cartesian algebra comparison and canonical relative-spectrum base change give an isomorphism $c_\alpha:P_y\simeq V\times_U P_x$. Define $\mathcal Y(U)$ to have objects $(x,s)$, where $s:U\to P_x$ is a section. An arrow $(y,t)\to(x,s)$ over $u$ is an arrow $\alpha:y\to x$ of $\mathcal X$ for which $c_\alpha\circ t=(1_V,s\circ u)$. Identities and composites are those of $\mathcal X$: the corresponding comparisons agree because both induce the same composite pullback algebra map under the affine-algebra anti-equivalence. Pulling back $s$ using $c_\alpha^{-1}$ supplies cartesian lifts. Consequently this is a category fibred in groupoids with a projection $q:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$. This constructs the data, without choosing them from an existence theorem.

source.place: Tags 01LS (lemma-spec-base-change) and 01LX (lemma-spec-properties)(2); explicit Grothendieck construction of the relative section groupoids.

proof.text: Fix $x\in\mathcal X(U)$. For a test scheme $v:V\to U$, an object of $U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Y$ is $(y,t,\alpha:y\simeq v^*x)$. Its section $t$ transports to a section of $V\times_U P_x$, hence to a $U$-map $V\to P_x$. Conversely such a map gives the section over $v^*x$ and the identity comparison. An arrow in this relative fibre must preserve the specified comparison $\alpha$, so it is unique when the maps $V\to P_x$ agree, and nonexistent otherwise. These mutually inverse descriptions commute with pullback. Thus $U\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Y\simeq h_{P_x}$ over $U$ and its projection is the affine scheme morphism $P_x\to U$. Since $\mathcal X$ is an etale stack, the representable-fibred-category stack lemma now proves that $\mathcal Y$ is an etale stack.

source.place: Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic), stack assertion, after the explicit scheme-base-change identification from Constructions Tag 01LX.

proof.text: For the atlas object $a\in\mathcal X(T)$, $\lambda$ gives $P_a\simeq Z$ by the affine-algebra anti-equivalence. The comparison of step 5 therefore identifies $T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Y$ with $Z$. On $T_2$ the induced transport on algebras is $\delta$, so transport on spectra has pullback map $\delta^{-1}=\theta^\sharp$; the affine-algebra functor is faithful, hence the transport is exactly the specified $\theta$. Thus the datum has been recovered, rather than just its underlying finite scheme.

source.place: Tag 01SA (lemma-affine-equivalence-algebras), faithfulness and base-change compatibility, with stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06WV(1).

proof.text: Fix $x\in\mathcal X(U)$ with $U$ a scheme. The 2-fibre product $E=U\times_{\mathcal X}T$ is an algebraic space by the DM diagonal convention. Choose jointly surjective etale scheme charts $U_i\to E$. The atlas test in the stack conventions says that their composites $U_i\to U$ form a jointly surjective etale family. Each chart includes a map $t_i:U_i\to T$ and the 2-comparison $x|_{U_i}\simeq a\circ t_i$. Thus steps 5--6 identify the scheme $P_x\times_UU_i$ with $Z\times_TU_i$ over $U_i$. The latter is finite by the finite-morphism clause of the base-change lemma. Apply the finer-topology lemma with base scheme $T=U$ and final object $U$ of $U_{\mathrm{et}}$: its covering-family hypothesis is exactly the family just obtained, so this family is an fpqc covering. The finiteness-descent lemma now applies to the scheme morphism $P_x\to U$ and these finite scheme base changes, proving it finite. This proves finite scheme representability for every $x$. Neither scheme representability of $E$ nor quasi-compactness of the given atlas is required.

source.place: Tag 02LA (lemma-descending-property-finite); Topologies Tag 022C (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc); scheme base-change stability of finiteness.

proof.text: Given a compatible map $Z\to Z'$ of the input data, the affine-algebra anti-equivalence gives $M'\to M$ commuting with descent. Fullness of module descent supplies a unique map $\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$. It is an algebra map because its unit and multiplication equations can be tested after restriction to $T$, where they hold. For every $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, relative spectrum gives $P_x\to P'_x$; these maps commute with cartesian pullback by base-change compatibility, and hence define $(x,s)\mapsto(x,h_xs)$ on the constructed groupoids. Faithfulness of the two equivalences gives uniqueness up to the unique 2-isomorphism over $\mathcal X$. Conversely a map over $\mathcal X$ pulls back to scheme maps $P_x\to P'_x$; their algebra maps are cartesian and are determined by restriction to $T$. Therefore pullback is fully faithful, including non-invertible morphisms. Hom sets in the representable slice are taken up to 2-isomorphism; their relative fibres are discrete, as checked in step 5.

source.place: Tag 01SA (lemma-affine-equivalence-algebras), all morphisms; stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06WV(1), fullness and faithfulness on module maps.

proof.text: To check recovery for an arbitrary representable finite $q_0:\mathcal Y_0\to\mathcal X$, form its finite scheme base change $P^0_x\to U$ for every $x\in\mathcal X(U)$. The algebras $(P^0_x\to U)_*\mathcal O_{P^0_x}$ are quasi-coherent, and the canonical affine base-change isomorphisms make them a cartesian algebra assignment. Restriction to $T$ is exactly the algebra of the pulled-back finite scheme with its canonical descent datum. Module descent and its faithfulness identify the algebra reconstructed in steps 2--3 with this assignment. Step 5 then identifies the constructed fibre over every $x$ with $P^0_x$, naturally. Explicitly, an object $y\in\mathcal Y_0(U)$ determines $x=q_0(y)$ and the section of $P^0_x$ represented by $(y,\operatorname{id}_x)$. Conversely a section is a relative-fibre object $(y,\alpha:q_0(y)\simeq x)$, so gives an object of $\mathcal Y_0(U)$ with its comparison to $x$. Arrows are precisely arrows of $\mathcal Y_0$ preserving these comparisons, by the definition of the 2-fibre product. The two constructions are inverse up to the specified comparison, and commute with base pullbacks. Thus $\mathcal Y_0\simeq\mathcal Y$ over $\mathcal X$. Together with steps 6 and 8 this proves the asserted categorical equivalence.

source.place: Tag 01SA (lemma-affine-equivalence-algebras) and Constructions Tag 01LX(2),(3), applied to the scheme fibres; stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06WV(1).

proof.text: The hypotheses of the existing representable-finite stack lemma now hold: $\mathcal X$ is DM, $\mathcal Y$ is a stack by step 5, and $q$ is representable finite by step 7. Its DM conclusion applies. Moreover $Z\simeq T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Y$ is a surjective etale scheme atlas: for every $U\to\mathcal Y$ its base change is $U\times_{\mathcal X}T\to U$, the test already required of the original atlas $a$. If $Z$ has normal local rings, this very atlas is a normal etale atlas of $\mathcal Y$, which is precisely the asserted meaning of normality. This last inference is definitional; it does not require normality of $\mathcal X$ or a theorem about normalization.

lean.statement: theorem finiteSchemes_etale_stack_descent (S : Scheme.{u}) (X : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hX : IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack X) (T : Over S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) X) (ha : IsEtaleModuliAtlas a) : (finiteStackRestriction a).IsEquivalence ∧ (∀ P : FiniteStackSections X, IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack (stackSectionTotal P.obj) ∧ IsRepresentableFiniteModuliMap (stackSectionProjection P.obj) ∧ (∀ (Z : Over S) (p : Z ⟶ T), IsFinite p.left → Nonempty (a.toFunctor.op ⋙ P.obj ≅ finiteSchemeSections p) → (∀ z : Z.left, IsDomain (Z.left.presheaf.stalk z) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Z.left.presheaf.stalk z)) → ∃ (U : Over S) (b : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) (stackSectionTotal P.obj)), IsEtaleModuliAtlas b ∧ ∀ z : U.left, IsDomain (U.left.presheaf.stalk z) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (U.left.presheaf.stalk z))) ∧ (∀ (Y : BasedCategory.{v', w'} (Over S)) (q : BasedFunctor Y X), IsFibredInGroupoids Y → IsRepresentableFiniteModuliMap q → ∃ (P : FiniteStackSections X) (e : BasedFunctor Y (stackSectionTotal P.obj)), e.toFunctor.IsEquivalence ∧ Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (e.comp (stackSectionProjection P.obj)) q)) ∧ (∀ (P Q : FiniteStackSections X) (f : BasedFunctor (stackSectionTotal P.obj) (stackSectionTotal Q.obj)) (β : ModuliTwoIso (f.comp (stackSectionProjection Q.obj)) (stackSectionProjection P.obj)), ∃! η : P.obj ⟶ Q.obj, ∃ γ : ModuliTwoIso f (stackSectionMap η), ∀ z : (stackSectionTotal P.obj).obj, (stackSectionProjection Q.obj).map (γ.val.hom.app z) = β.val.hom.app z)
